subject: Copywriting
title: Political Advertising
description: Learn Political Advertising in one minute.

hook.text: The 1964 'Daisy' ad showed a girl picking petals before a nuclear explosion.

buildup.text: The ad never mentioned Barry Goldwater by name. It implied voting for him meant nuclear war.

discovery.text: Political ads use advertising techniques—emotional appeals, simple messages, fear—to sell candidates exactly like.

twist.text: Citizens United (2010) allowed unlimited political ad spending.

climax.text: In 2020, US political campaigns spent $14 billion on advertising.

punchline.text: $14 billion on political ads. Democracy's copy has a price tag.

quiz.question: What did the 1964 'Daisy' ad imply?
options: Voting for Goldwater meant nuclear war
